body.title: Specify an experimental ledger of contributions and accountability
body.body:
## What is delivered
A specification for an experimental ledger: contributions, needs, decisions and accountability. Who takes part, what the unit of record is, who reviews it, and what ends the experiment.

An accounting exercise. Deliberately.

## Why it is needed
The order of work here is the thing most likely to be got wrong. The first validation is an accounting one, not a monetary one — a transparent record of what was contributed, what was needed and what was decided, before anything moves and before any unit exists to move.

Nothing internally demonstrates monetary policy, liquidity, audit or financial governance, and this component does not promise income, return or support payments to anyone. A ledger is what makes the rest possible to argue about honestly.

## Where to start
"Unit of record" does not mean currency. Hours, deliveries, commitments met — the question is what can be recorded consistently enough that two people reading the ledger agree on what happened.

Whatever this becomes, it stays inside the limits on the economy page: no token, no exchange, no return.

## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/fn/

body.title: Frame value as member-governed common capacity
body.body: Replaces the automatic contribution-to-access chain with accountable member governance. Makes Dk responsible for evidence, modelling and recommendations rather than allocation, and strengthens the boundary against score-based entitlement.

body.title: Weight in member choices instead of voting weight
body.body_html:
Aligns this repository with the decisions of October 2026:

  • member councils formed for each question instead of an independent judicial panel chosen by lot;
  • no forks or open-code claims for Dk: auditable through Dknowledge and DFM by permission level, with divergence tested in parallel;
  • Dk Global decides only inside the space the constitution gives it, open to representation, proposals and justified vetoes;
  • units of account instead of a token economy.

body.title: Financing earns the reward; floor support lives in Distributed Support
body.body:
- Money still cannot buy member status, the reputation of work or weight in member choices.
- **Financing the network earns the reward**, a transferable reputation that can give faster or priority access to resources. "Priority" is no longer listed as something money can never reach, because financing reaches it through the reward.
- The non-scope line no longer denies any guarantee of support: support for approved members through the common floor is specified in Distributed Support. Yield, appreciation, liquidity and income stay excluded.

Founder decisions (06/10/2026): "quem financia também ganha essa mesma reputação" and "O piso comum é para membros aprovados".

body.title: docs: Dk Global decides allocations inside the constitution, members can veto
body.body:
## Founder decisions (06/10/2026)
- "no resto o Dk global decide e executa autonomamente"
- "Com os membros podendo fazer o veto bem justificado."
  (Outside the constitution, Dk Global decides and executes autonomously; members can make a well-justified veto, which obliges review.)
- On Autonomous Health: "o sistema está integrado ao Dk pessoal e ao dknowledge da pessoa, mais seus dispositivos, padrões que podem estar conectados a algo com probabilidade suficiente são investigados… além de salvar vidas também aprimora a detecção multifator de todo tipo de condição."
- Timeline: "a 1.0 já vai ser uma ASI, mas como singularidade, precisará de recursos suficientes e isso talvez aconteça até 2033."

## Allocation authority
- `README.md:23`: "Dk models scenarios, but human member governance decides allocations inside systemic safeguards." → "Dk models scenarios and decides allocations autonomously inside the constitution and its systemic safeguards, and members can make a well-justified veto."
- `README.md:42`: "- Automated allocation by Dk without constitutional rules, human authorization and review" → "- Automated allocation by Dk outside the constitution, its systemic safeguards or the review that a well-justified member veto obliges"
- `.drayker/component.yml:25` (same non-scope item): "Automated allocation by Dk without constitutional rules, accountable authorization and review." → "Automated allocation by Dk outside the constitution, its systemic safeguards or the review that a well-justified member veto obliges." (YAML validated). The portal mirror is updated in drayker.org.

body.title: Common floor support is for members, not approved members
body.body:
## What changed
- **component.yml, non_scope:** "Support for approved members through the common floor" becomes "Support for members through the common floor".

## Why
Membership needs no approval: anyone becomes a member by being a person and creating their UID. The common floor belongs to every member, with a context-weighted queue while resources are scarce (see draykerdk/distributed-support). Mirrored on drayker.org and drayker.com.
